title: SQS: work delivery, visibility, and deletion
outcome: Set up a queue and dead-letter path and implement repeat-safe processing.
drawbacks: Visibility, duplicate effects, and DLQ recovery still need design.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: Receive. Do durable work. Delete. Expect repeats.

trace.title: Queue message
trace.detail: A queue hands work to consumers. Receiving an SQS message does not remove it; visibility temporarily hides it under the queue’s contract. Successful processing is followed by deliberate deletion using the receipt handle. If processing fails or times out, work can be seen again.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Send → visible → receive → temporarily invisible → DB effect → delete. Crash after DB commit but before delete leads to repetition, which a unique event/command identity must tolerate.

DLQ means quarantined for investigation, not successfully processed. Redrive after a repair needs a repeat-safe consumer and an understanding of ordering consequences.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Deleting before processing can lose work. A too-short visibility window can overlap processing. A long visibility value can delay recovery after a real crash.
